commits.pr_title: chore(ci): close PRs with unverified commits after 14 days
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Automatically close PRs that still have unsigned commits two weeks after the signed-commits bot flagged them.

### New: `signed-commits-close.yml`

Runs daily at 00:20 UTC (also manually via `workflow_dispatch`, which defaults to **dry run**).

1. Lists open PRs carrying the `blocked by: unverified commits` label. Only labelled PRs are ever considered.
2. Reads each PR's issue events to find when the label was last applied. The 14-day clock starts there, not at last activity, so discussion on the PR does not delay closure.
3. Skips PRs flagged fewer than 14 days ago.
4. Re-checks the commits with the same `verification.reason === "unsigned"` test as `signed-commits.yml`. If they are all signed now, it removes the label instead of closing.
5. Otherwise posts a closing comment and closes the PR.

Independent of `issue-stale.yml` / `actions/stale`. Uses only `pull-requests: write`.

### Changed: `signed-commits.yml`

- Bot comment now ends with: *"Note: this PR will be closed automatically if the commits are not signed within 14 days."*
- The bot recognises its own comment by the opening sentence instead of an exact body match, so comments already posted on open PRs continue to be found and cleaned up.

### Label lifecycle

- Label added by `signed-commits.yml` when unsigned commits are pushed.
- Label removed by `signed-commits.yml` as soon as a push makes all commits verified (also on `reopened`).
- Label also removed by the new workflow if it finds the commits signed during its daily pass.

## Before merging

The first scheduled run will close every PR that has carried the label for 14+ days, including ones flagged long ago. Recommended: merge, then trigger a manual dry run and review the log before the first scheduled run.

commits.pr_title: fix(registry): keep @voraui logo arcs unfilled in the directory
commits.pr_body:
Follow-up to #11172.

The directory renders logos with `*:[svg]:fill-foreground`, which overrides the root `fill='none'` attribute on the @voraui logo. Its paths are stroke-only arcs and inherit that fill, so they render as a solid black dome instead of three outlined arcs.

### Changes

getRegistryStyles, getRegistryIcons and fetchTree call handleError, which

Rename-only commit: moves src/registry, src/schema and every module they
reach (the install pipeline behind addRegistryItems), their tests,
snapshots, test helpers and fixtures from packages/shadcn to
packages/registry with the same paths. The next commit wires it up.

* feat(registry): add the @shadcn/registry package

shadcn now depends on @shadcn/registry instead of bundling the registry
code. shadcn/registry and shadcn/schema re-export the package, and CLI
code imports the moved modules through @shadcn/registry/internal/*.

- Every module is a build entry, so shared state (registry context, fetch
  cache, spinners) lives in one chunk and exists once per process.
- shadcn's vitest resolves @shadcn/registry to source, so mocks of
  registry modules in CLI tests apply to the registry's own imports.
- Test fixtures move with the tests that use them; CLI tests read them
  from packages/registry/test/fixtures.

* chore(registry): build, test and release @shadcn/registry

- Add a changeset: @shadcn/registry starts at 0.1.0, shadcn gets a patch.
- Build shadcn's dependencies first (--filter=shadcn...) and make
  typecheck depend on ^build, since shadcn's types come from the
  registry's declarations.
- Templates workflow: bun and yarn cannot resolve workspace:, so stage a
  shadcn package that depends on a packed @shadcn/registry tarball.
- Check shadcn's public exports in CI.
- Wait for the registry build in the e2e setup.
- Document the new package in RELEASING.md.

* fix(registry): address review findings

- Declare @babel/preset-typescript in @shadcn/registry, as shadcn does:
  @babel/core requires it by name, so bundling the registry on its own
  failed to resolve it.
- Keep the published declarations to declared packages: type-fest is now
  a dependency (it only ships types), and update-tailwind-config uses a
  local stand-in for tailwindcss's Config with the same shape.
- pub:* scripts build @shadcn/registry first and refuse to publish shadcn
  while the @shadcn/registry version it pins is not on npm.
- shadcn:test also runs the @shadcn/registry tests.
- Docs: new-package publishing bootstrap and the @shadcn/registry
  changeset rule in RELEASING.md, the dev command and package layout in

* test: resolve @shadcn/registry to source in the root vitest config

The root vitest workspace (used by editors and bare `vitest` runs) did
not alias @shadcn/registry, so tests run that way loaded the registry's
build and mocks of registry modules could not reach calls made inside it.
Share the source aliases between the root and shadcn configs.

* ci: never publish a shadcn with a broken @shadcn/registry dependency

changeset publish publishes every package in parallel, so a failed
@shadcn/registry publish could leave a shadcn on npm pinned to a version
that does not exist.

Both release jobs now publish with .github/changeset-publish.js, which:
1. publishes everything except the packages that depend on
   @shadcn/registry,
2. checks that the registry version they pin is on npm, and that it was
   released from the current registry source (via its release tag),
3. only then publishes shadcn.

Add a pull request check that fails when the registry source changes
without an @shadcn/registry changeset, so releases do not stall on the
second check.

* ci: make the registry publish checks fail closed

- Only a 404 from npm counts as unpublished; other lookup errors stop the
  release instead of skipping a check.
- Only package.json fields that change the published package count as a
  registry change, so devDependency and script updates (Dependabot) do

* ci: harden the @shadcn/registry release guard

From an adversarial review of the publish guard:

  array. CI installs npm@latest (12.x), where the guard would otherwise
  have blocked every shadcn release.
- On stable releases, always check the registry version against its git
  tag instead of inferring that this run published it, push a tag this
  run created right away, and explain how to recover a missing tag.
- Run releases and prereleases one at a time.
- Match tests and snapshots anywhere under packages/registry/src, and
  count the bundled @antfu/ni and tinyexec as registry source.
- Drop the branch-name exemption from the PR check: the version PR

changeset version uses @changesets/changelog-github, which needs a token
to read pull request info. Without one the snapshot step fails before
anything is published, so no prerelease has published since the switch
to changeset version --snapshot.

The first beta took about 80 seconds for @shadcn/registry and about five
minutes for shadcn to be served by npm. Give the registry check room as
the package gets busier, instead of failing the release.

There is no breaking change for `shadcn` users. `shadcn/registry` and `shadcn/schema` re-export the new package, and every other entry point keeps the same exports.

- `@shadcn/registry`: the registry API (fetch, resolve, search, install items).
- `@shadcn/registry/schema`: the registry, item and `components.json` schemas.
